bio: Mapouginen is the artistic alias of Montreal multidisciplinary artist and choreographer Cindy Belotte. Her work is rooted in Montreal's Black and diasporic arts communities, and the Mapouginen name also appears among the performers on the large-scale Quebec recording Stand By Me/Lean On Me. Northern Dial carries Mapouginen as part of its Montreal multidisciplinary and vocal arts catalogue.
Thetford Mines singer-songwriter Marco Ema is a Québec indie-pop and rock artist whose nostalgic, coming-of-age writing mixes melodic pop with increasingly raw guitar-driven production.
Edmonton-born singer-songwriter Maren Ord is a Canadian pop and rock artist whose early-2000s career included national radio success and a Juno nomination for Best New Artist.

Toronto-born R&B and soul singer-songwriter Maria-Therese is a Canadian artist whose work pairs intimate storytelling with themes of resilience, healing and personal growth. Her releases have reached CBC, BBC Radio, SiriusXM and major streaming platforms, while the Warner Music Canada-released EP MONARCH marked a major step in her contemporary R&B career.

Vancouver's Marianas Trench grew from the mid-2000s Canadian pop-rock circuit into a band defined by unusually elaborate vocal arrangements, narrative album structures and the studio ambition of singer, songwriter and producer Josh Ramsay. The 2006 debut Fix Me established the group, but Masterpiece Theatre and Ever After turned that foundation into a distinctive style built around stacked harmonies, recurring musical themes and songs designed to work both as radio singles and pieces of larger album-length arcs.

Ever After became a major Canadian commercial breakthrough, producing songs including "Haven't Had Enough," "Fallout" and "Stutter" and earning JUNO nominations for Album of the Year and Pop Album of the Year. The band continued the theatrical approach on Astoria and Phantoms, while Ramsay's work outside the group further extended its influence: he co-wrote and produced Carly Rae Jepsen's global hit "Call Me Maybe." Marianas Trench's longevity has been especially notable in Canada, where the band built a multi-platinum catalogue and a large touring audience without abandoning increasingly elaborate arrangements.

The sixth album Haven arrived in 2024, using the hero's-journey framework as the basis for another heavily orchestrated concept record. Across nearly two decades, Marianas Trench has occupied an unusual place between pop-punk, mainstream pop and progressive-minded studio craft. Their significance comes from making maximalism part of their identity: big choruses and radio accessibility coexist with long-form sequencing, orchestration and vocal construction that reward listening beyond the singles.

Marie Celeste is a Quebec group originating in Alma, Lac-Saint-Jean and later associated with Montreal's independent scene. The band's music draws together folk, indie rock, jazz and experimental textures around francophone songwriting. Northern Dial carries Marie Celeste as part of its Quebec independent music catalogue.
Montréal producer and musician Marie Davidson makes dark, sharply observational electronic music, moving between techno, minimal wave, Italo disco and spoken-word performance.

Haiti-born, Québec-raised soprano Marie-Josée Lord is a Canadian opera singer whose acclaimed stage career and best-selling classical recordings have earned multiple Félix awards and a Juno nomination.
Québec singer-songwriter Marie-Mai is a major francophone Canadian pop artist whose high-energy catalogue blends pop, rock and electronic music and has earned numerous Félix awards.
Roxton Pond singer and radio host Marie-Ève Janvier is a Canadian francophone vocalist whose career spans musical theatre, solo recordings and popular Québec media.

Halifax rapper Markit, born Mark Cwajna, emerged from Nova Scotia's independent hip-hop scene as a member of Fax4 before expanding into solo work and the group Something Good with Boy-Ill. His 2007 album Mark My Words helped earn national exposure, including a VideoFACT-supported MuchMusic video with fellow Fax4 member Spesh K.

Markus Aurelyus is a Scarborough-based Trinidadian-Canadian singer-songwriter whose music blends R&B, soul, gospel, pop and hip-hop influences. His work reflects both his Caribbean heritage and Toronto-area upbringing. Northern Dial carries Markus Aurelyus as part of its contemporary Canadian R&B and soul catalogue.
Montréal-born singer Martine St-Clair is a Canadian francophone pop artist whose career began in Starmania before expanding into a long run of successful Québec solo albums.

Toronto rapper Marvel is a veteran of the city's early independent hip-hop movement and a member of the Circle crew and Figurez of Speech. Closely connected to artists including Kardinal Offishall, Choclair and Solitair, he built a solo catalogue around releases such as No Streets (Just the World), combining Toronto-focused writing with production from some of Canada's best-known hip-hop producers.
Lebanese-born Canadian singer-songwriter Massari built an Ottawa-rooted R&B and pop career around melodic vocals, Middle Eastern influence and international crossover singles.
Toronto DJ, broadcaster and programmer Mastermind, born Paul Parhar, is a foundational Canadian hip-hop curator whose mixtapes and radio work helped document and promote the country's rap scene.
Toronto rapper, producer and DJ Mathematik, born Lyndon Dash, is a Canadian underground hip-hop artist known for jazz-inflected production, conscious lyricism and his connection to Down Ta Erf.
Manitoba-born singer-songwriter Matt Epp is a Canadian roots, rock and soul artist known for confessional writing, international touring and award-winning songwriting.
Nova Scotia singer-songwriter Matt Mays is a Canadian rock artist whose solo work and recordings with El Torpedo blend heartland rock, alternative rock and expansive guitar-driven songwriting.

Burnaby-born singer-songwriter Matthew Good became one of the defining voices of late-1990s Canadian alternative rock through the Matthew Good Band. The group's independent 1995 debut Last of the Ghetto Astronauts established an unusually strong foothold outside the major-label system, while 1997's Underdogs delivered the breakthrough singles "Apparitions" and "Everything Is Automatic." Good's writing paired large guitar hooks with a more restless, literate tone than much of the era's post-grunge radio, helping the band stand apart as Canadian modern rock was becoming a national mainstream format.

Beautiful Midnight pushed that momentum to its peak in 1999. The album debuted at No. 1 in Canada, produced staples including "Hello Time Bomb," "Load Me Up" and "Strange Days," and won the 2000 JUNO Award for Best Rock Album. The darker The Audio of Being became the band's final studio record before Good moved into a solo career with Avalanche in 2003. He continued to change scale and texture through White Light Rock & Roll Review, Hospital Music and Vancouver, with the latter winning the 2011 JUNO for Rock Album of the Year. Later records such as Lights of Endangered Species, Arrows of Desire and Moving Walls kept his catalogue moving between full-band alternative rock, orchestral arrangements and more stripped-back songwriting.

Good's importance to Canadian music comes from sustaining two substantial careers without simply repeating the Matthew Good Band formula. His catalogue spans the commercial peak of 1990s Canadian alternative radio and a long solo period defined by stylistic shifts, politically and socially observant writing and a willingness to make increasingly personal records. More than three decades after his first independent release, he remains active: in September 2026, Good wrote on his official site that he had begun recording another album in Toronto, continuing a career that has remained closely tied to Canadian rock even as its surrounding industry has changed.

Matthew Good Band emerged from the Vancouver-area alternative-rock scene in the mid-1990s and became one of Canada’s dominant rock-radio acts around the turn of the millennium. Built around singer-songwriter Matthew Good, the group first attracted national attention with Last of the Ghetto Astronauts before 1997’s Underdogs produced enduring Canadian alternative staples including “Apparitions” and “Everything Is Automatic.”

Beautiful Midnight expanded the band’s sound and commercial reach through “Hello Time Bomb,” “Load Me Up” and “Strange Days.” The album won the 2000 JUNO Award for Best Rock Album, while the band won Best Group, confirming its place near the centre of Canadian alternative rock at the time. The Audio of Being followed in 2001, after which the group dissolved and Good continued under his own name.

Although the band’s run was relatively short, its impact was concentrated. Matthew Good Band helped define the darker, literate side of late-1990s Canadian rock, balancing large radio choruses with anxious social commentary and a more confrontational lyrical voice. Its catalogue remains distinct from Good’s later solo work and captures a specific period when Canadian alternative bands could become national stars largely through domestic radio, MuchMusic and touring.
Toronto multidisciplinary artist Matthew Progress creates Canadian experimental hip-hop, electronic music, film and performance work shaped by surrealism, Black culture and social commentary.

Mattmac, born Matthew Monias, is an Oji-Cree singer, rapper and producer from Garden Hill First Nation in northern Manitoba. Blind from birth, he grew up surrounded by music, sang in his community gospel choir and taught himself beat-making, piano and guitar. His first major public step came through the N’we Jinan mobile studio program, which visited Garden Hill in 2016 and helped him record "Help You See," a song built from his own experience and community perspective.

His 2020 debut project 20/20 pushed that story into a broader national audience. The single "Paradise" reached No. 1 on the Indigenous Music Countdown, and Mattmac’s combination of melodic hooks, hip-hop production and autobiographical writing brought him media attention across Canada. He later won Rap/Electronic Album of the Year at the 2021 Summer Solstice Indigenous Music Awards and continued expanding his catalogue with collaborations, including work connected to artists such as Nelly Furtado and Drezus.

Mattmac’s significance extends beyond an inspirational narrative. He is part of a generation of Indigenous artists using contemporary pop, rap and production tools without separating those sounds from community, place or identity. His career also broadens assumptions about who gets to be a producer and recording artist, making his presence in Northern Dial’s catalogue important both musically and culturally.
Saint-Georges, Québec singer-songwriter Maxime Landry is a Canadian francophone artist who broke nationally after winning Star Académie in 2009 and went on to earn multiple Félix awards.
Lawrence Heights rapper Mayhem Morearty is a Canadian hip-hop artist from Toronto whose autobiographical street rap grew from the Hustlemann collective and the city's independent scene.
Lawrence Heights rapper Mayhem Morearty is a Canadian hip-hop artist from Toronto whose autobiographical street rap grew from the Hustlemann collective and the city's independent scene.
Toronto multidisciplinary artist Maylee Todd is a singer, songwriter, producer and performance artist known for adventurous work that moves between soul, electronic music and experimental pop.

MayOne-9 is a Canadian hip-hop artist associated with Toronto rap group BrassMunk and with producer Dub J's early-2000s Canadian hip-hop network. His work sits within the same era that connected artists such as JD Era, Eternia, D-Sisive and Moka Only. Northern Dial carries MayOne-9 as part of Canada's 2000s underground rap history.

Egyptian-Canadian singer, songwriter, producer and instrumentalist Maz B is a Winnipeg-based R&B artist whose moody, contemporary sound has made him an emerging voice in Canada's independent soul scene.

McMaster is the split Northern Dial credit for Canadian singer-songwriter Luke McMaster, one half of Winnipeg pop and R&B duo McMaster & James with Rob James. The duo's gold-selling Canadian run produced radio hits including Thank You, the exact McMaster credit represented in the Northern Dial library.

Fredericton-born Canadian soprano Measha Brueggergosman-Lee is an internationally acclaimed opera and concert singer whose recordings and performances also span jazz, gospel and contemporary repertoire.

Meeno Giinchy is a Mississauga hip-hop artist and collaborator active in the Greater Toronto Area rap scene. His catalogue includes solo releases and collaborations with artists from Toronto and surrounding communities, placing him within Southern Ontario's independent hip-hop network. Northern Dial carries Meeno Giinchy as part of its GTA hip-hop catalogue.

Meesah is a Pickering, Ontario R&B singer and songwriter whose independent catalogue reaches back to the mid-2000s. Her work centres on smooth contemporary R&B, with releases and collaborations spanning Canada's independent soul and pop ecosystem. Northern Dial carries Meesah as part of its Durham Region and Greater Toronto Area R&B catalogue.
Bowmanville, Ontario singer-songwriter Meghan Patrick is a Canadian country artist known for a tough, rootsy sound, emotionally direct writing and multiple CCMA and CMAOntario honours.

Montréal singer-songwriter and vocal producer Mel Pacifico is a Canadian R&B artist whose silky vocals, layered harmonies and contemporary soul production position her among the country's emerging R&B voices.
Nova Scotia-born singer-songwriter and multi-instrumentalist Melanie Doane is a Juno-winning Canadian pop-rock artist whose career also spans theatre, television and music education.
Toronto singer-songwriter Melanie Durrant makes soulful R&B and alternative hip-hop soul, pairing formal vocal training with an eclectic sound and a long-running independent Canadian career.

Toronto-born Melanie Fiona developed through the city's R&B scene before finding a larger international audience with a sound built around classic soul phrasing and contemporary production. After early work in the Canadian group X-Quisite and years of writing and performing, she joined Kanye West's European tour in 2008, giving her a major international stage before her debut album arrived. The Bridge followed in 2009, blending retro-soul references with modern R&B and producing "Give It to Me Right" and the breakthrough ballad "It Kills Me."

"It Kills Me" brought Fiona her first Grammy nomination and helped establish The Bridge as more than a stylistic throwback. Her second album, The MF Life, widened the palette through collaborations and more contemporary production, while the CeeLo Green duet "Fool for You" became a major awards moment. Fiona won two Grammys for the song, including Best Traditional R&B Performance and Best R&B Song, and later received another nomination for "Wrong Side of a Love Song." Those honours placed a Toronto-born singer squarely inside the U.S. R&B awards establishment.

Fiona's importance to Canadian music is tied to that cross-border credibility. She emerged before the current generation of Toronto R&B stars had made the city a global brand, yet her success showed that a Canadian vocalist could enter the American soul tradition on equal footing rather than as a novelty export. Her catalogue also connects different generations of R&B, drawing from Motown and classic soul while remaining grounded in the production language of the 2000s and 2010s.
Toronto artist and producer Memblem, also known as Michael Emblem, makes Canadian electronic and genre-blurring music and has earned support from producers including Timbaland and Kenny Beats.
Toronto-based Palestinian-Canadian singer, songwriter and producer Merna Bishouty, formerly known as Ayah, makes soul and R&B and has collaborated across Canadian and international hip-hop.
Gatineau singer-songwriter Mia Kelly is a Canadian bilingual folk, rock and blues artist known for poetic writing, a versatile voice and extensive touring in Canada and abroad.

Mia Martina grew up in Saint-Ignace, New Brunswick, and entered the music business from the label side, initially interning at CP Records before moving into backing vocals and eventually becoming a front-line artist. That route gave her a practical understanding of the machinery behind pop releases, but her own breakthrough was immediate: the 2010 single "Stereo Love" became a double-platinum Canadian hit and introduced her as a dance-pop vocalist with a strong connection to European club music.

Her 2011 debut album Devotion extended that momentum into international markets, particularly across Europe, while later singles including "Burning," "Latin Moon," "Heartbreaker" and "Danse" kept her visible on Canadian dance radio. Martina's trilingual background and global-facing production distinguished her from many domestic pop acts of the period. Universal Music Canada noted three consecutive JUNO nominations for Dance Recording of the Year, while "Danse" achieved gold status and further connected her to the cross-border EDM and pop scene.

Martina's Canadian significance is less about dominating one era than about representing a specific early-2010s moment when club music became mainstream pop. From a small New Brunswick community, she built a career that moved naturally through Toronto label infrastructure and into European dance markets. Her catalogue captures the period when Canadian pop increasingly became borderless, digitally distributed and comfortable borrowing from international club culture rather than treating domestic radio as the final destination.

Mic Check is an Ottawa-based French-language rapper who appeared with DL Incognito on 'Savoir Faire' from the 2002 album A Sample and a Drum Machine and later on 'Fall Back.' Northern Dial's Mic Check entry is tied directly to that DL Incognito catalogue, and artist profiles identify Mic Check as representing Ottawa, Canada.

Burnaby-raised singer Michael Bublé is a Canadian pop, jazz and traditional-pop vocalist whose interpretations of standards and original songs have made him one of the country's most successful international artists.
Ottawa-born singer-songwriter Michelle Treacy is a Canadian pop artist known for emotionally direct songwriting, a breakout appearance with Lady Gaga and winning CTV's The Launch.

Born Michelle McCullock in Jamaica and raised in Toronto, Michie Mee began rapping professionally as a teenager and became one of the first Canadian MCs to build meaningful connections with the New York hip-hop industry. Her early work brought her into the orbit of Boogie Down Productions, and the 1987 single "Elements of Style" helped establish a voice that moved naturally between hip-hop, reggae and Jamaican patois. In 1988, she became the first Canadian rapper to sign with a major U.S. label, a breakthrough that arrived before Canada had a durable commercial infrastructure for domestic hip-hop.

Her 1991 debut album Jamaican Funk – Canadian Style made that cross-border and cross-Caribbean identity explicit. Rather than imitating an American rap template, Michie Mee placed dancehall phrasing, reggae rhythm and Toronto hip-hop inside the same frame, creating a sound that anticipated the Caribbean influence that would later become one of the most recognizable features of Toronto popular music. She continued to resist easy categorization through the 1990s, including a period with Raggadeath, whose mixture of reggae and heavy rock pushed her into another hybrid setting. Her second album, The First Cut Is the Deepest, arrived in 2000 and reaffirmed her place as a working rapper rather than only a historical first.

Michie Mee's importance to Canadian hip-hop is larger than a single milestone. She helped prove that a Canadian MC could participate in the wider North American rap economy while sounding unmistakably shaped by Toronto's Caribbean communities. Later honours have increasingly recognized that role: she has received lifetime and hall-of-fame awards within Canadian urban music, and in January 2026 Canada Post issued a commemorative stamp honouring her alongside Maestro Fresh Wes and Muzion as one of the country's hip-hop trailblazers. Her career is part of the foundation beneath the multilingual, Caribbean-influenced Toronto sound that later became internationally familiar.
Vancouver singer-songwriter Mikey Jose is a Canadian R&B, gospel and pop artist whose independent music career runs alongside academic work in neuroscience.

MikeZup is a Montreal-area rapper, songwriter and producer whose career grew out of Quebec's francophone street-rap scene. Active since his teens, the Laval artist built an independent catalogue around projects including the Omerta trilogy, Imprévu and Couleurs Primaires before continuing through his own 630MG label.

Mileena is a Toronto-based neo-soul and alternative R&B singer-songwriter whose music moves through bedroom pop, lo-fi, trip-hop and soulful electronic textures. Her self-titled debut and Time Spent Running EP established her in Toronto's independent scene, while her feature on Kai Banks and La Reezy's Too Deep For The Outro is her Northern Dial library credit.

Miranda is a Canadian R&B vocalist associated with producer Dub J's Q It Up Records network and frequently credited as part of Mystic & Miranda. Her work appears within a Canadian hip-hop and R&B catalogue that connected artists across Kitchener-Waterloo and Toronto. Northern Dial carries Miranda as part of that early-2000s Canadian scene.
